Café De Unie, Rotterdam

J. J. P. Oud’s 1925 café front, rebuilt in 1986: the building is a billboard of flat colored planes, yellow bars, and square capitals.

Source
archiweb: Café De Unie
Creator
J. J. P. Oud
Made
1924–1925 (original on the Coolsingel, destroyed 1940); reconstruction 1985–1986 on the Mauritsweg
Style
De Stijl (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Loud, commercial, planar
Evidence
Inspected a 2009 photograph of the reconstruction by “Ad” on Wikimedia Commons.jpg) (1920 × 2560 px, viewed at 1600 px). No image is stored. The photograph shows the 1986 reconstruction, not the 1925 building.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

The original building was destroyed on 14 May 1940. The existing facade is a reconstruction on a different street.

Context

Oud designed the café for the Coolsingel in Rotterdam in 1924–1925. It was destroyed on 14 May 1940 and reconstructed in 1985–1986 by the architect Carel Weeber on the Mauritsweg. archiweb.

archiweb names Theo van Doesburg as a co-author; this record does not rely on that claim.

Observed

  • A black band near the top carries “DE UNIE” in large light gray-blue capitals, with “CAFE” set vertically at both ends and a yellow bar above.
  • Below it a large red-orange plane carries raised lines that form nested right angles.
  • Yellow bars frame the upper window band and the lower windows; the lower windows have yellow inner frames.
  • A vertical sign reads “DE • UNIE” in blue capitals with a yellow strip; a tall blue sign at the left reads “CAFE RESTAURANT” twice.
  • The ground floor is framed in bright blue; the rest of the facade is white.
  • A dark later storey rises behind the facade, and ordinary brick buildings stand on both sides.

Why it belongs

The facade treats architecture as a graphic panel, which makes it the closest pre-war precedent for a De Stijl website or sign system.

The red is closer to orange in this photograph, which may reflect the reconstruction, weathering, or the camera.

Borrow

Build the name into the composition as one rectangular plane among others.

Use thin yellow bars as frames and dividers between larger black, red, and white planes.
